findings.evidence: The census says 'Checked individually: every one of has_label's ten call sites, both of set_terminal_label's, and restore_labels' one currently sits inside an if/&&/||/! context' (:463). has_label has ELEVEN call sites, not ten. Enumerated from the current tree: 2062, 2076, 3820, 3848, 3849, 3927, 3928, 3985, 4542, 4552, 4553. The one the count omits is qa-gate.sh:3820 — remove_label()'s tail statement `! has_label "$1" "$2"`, structurally unlike the other ten (it is has_label used as another helper's RETURN VALUE, not a condition inside a cmd_* function). Independent baseline: `git show HEAD:.claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh` also has eleven (1683, 1697, 3278, 3306, 3307, 3385, 3386, 3443, 3959, 3969, 3970), so the miscount predates this change set and was carried forward into text re-authored this round at 12:57:58Z rather than re-derived. The two adjacent counts in the same sentence ARE right: set_terminal_label has exactly 2 call sites (6616, 6914 — 2017/2033/2109 are string literals naming the function, not calls) and restore_labels exactly 1 (2084). THE OPERATIVE CONCLUSION IS UNAFFECTED AND I VERIFIED IT: all eleven sit in exempt contexts, including :3820 — probed directly, the `!` exempts has_label's body even when remove_label is itself invoked bare (BODY-CONTINUED at rc=0 for bare/if/|| forms), while the same shape without the `!` aborts at rc=7, so the probe discriminates. The guard at :3762 (`|| true`) is present regardless, so no live defect exists on any path. This is a cardinality error in a sentence that explicitly claims individual enumeration, not a false safety claim.
findings.description: Below risk_threshold=high, so it does not block. It is recorded rather than waived because it is the same failure mode R19-F1 blocked on, one order of magnitude smaller: a claim about a set asserted from the prior draft instead of re-counted against the tree. Cost to a future reader is bounded — they grep, find eleven, see ten, and must re-derive which site the census did not look at. Remedy is three words in three places: :463 'ten' -> 'eleven', :3734 '(10 of them' -> '(11 of them', :3743 'ten callers' -> 'eleven callers', and ideally one clause naming :3820 as the structurally different one so the next re-count starts from a complete list.

findings.evidence: The R19-F2 remedy paragraph argues this round's growth '(+71-95s depending which pair of figures is compared) is roughly half the prior round's (~147s)'. Every other number in that paragraph is sourced and arithmetically correct — I recomputed all of them: 900/771.35 = 1.16679 -> '1.167x'; 756.16/900 = 84.02% and 771.35/900 = 85.71% -> '84-86%'; 900-756.16 = 143.84 -> '144s'; and the '+71-95s' range is exactly the min/max over all four implementer/QA pairings (71.25, 79.56, 86.44, 94.75). '~147s' is the only figure with no derivation on file: grepping run-tests.sh, review-separation.test.sh and unrecorded-review-artifact.test.sh turns up no prior-round pair that yields it. The nearest documented candidate is the 849s -> ~1000s growth recorded at run-tests.sh:640-644, which is 151s.
findings.description: The conclusion survives any candidate base (79.56/147 = 0.54, 79.56/151 = 0.53 — 'roughly half' either way), so nothing downstream changes. Flagged against CONTRIBUTING.md's 'every number carries the command that produced it and the commit it was measured at', in a paragraph that is otherwise a model of that rule.

I checked: all 11 have mtimes of 2026-08-27/08-28, roughly seventeen days before this change set, and their task ids are mktemp-shaped (approve_XXXXXX_KfqBGyjet7-21e etc).
